title: predictive-slot-leasing-and-graceful-defer-controller
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Context: Dedicated pools need predictable minimum throughput guarantees for paying tenants while maximizing overall utilization. Current admission controls are reactive (reject or soft-shed) and have limited visibility into near-term demand, which causes oscillation between heavy shedding and conservative autoscaler behavior. Problem: sudden tenant spikes either cause hard rejections or trigger large autoscaler scale-ups with slow ramp time. We need a solution that: 1) provides short-term minimum throughput contracts (soft-guarantees) per tenant/route, 2) reduces noisy autoscaler reactions by exposing short-window reserved slot signals, and 3) degrades tenant traffic gracefully with clear client guidance and fast retry semantics. Proposal summary: Implement a predictive slot-lease controller that issues time-limited 'throughput leases' to tenants. Leases are small, fixed-duration allocations of request permits (e.g., 1s or 5s windows) issued based on recent consumption + short-term demand prediction (exponential smoothing + weight for last N seconds). Key behaviors: - Lease issuance: per-tenant/route/model policy calculates required baseline slots and grants leases up to a configured soft-floor. - Fast-path bursts: small low-latency bursts (<= X tokens/req or <= Y ms exec) are allowed through a separate fast-path queue to avoid latency amplification. - Staged defer policy: when pool approaches capacity, new requests are deferred with a staged Retry-After that includes suggested alternatives (lower-cost model, smaller sequence length, or queued-defer token). - Lease reclamation: controller can revoke or shrink leases mid-duration under sustained overload; clients receive structured HTTP 202/421 with a lease token and a suggested next attempt window. - Autoscaler integration: leases emit an aggregated short-window utilization metric (leased_util_pct) and an headroom signal to the autoscaler to avoid overreacting to transient spikes. - Observability: lease issuance, revocation, and deferred decision events are instrumented with per-tenant dashboards and a lineage id for traceability. Why different from existing approaches: instead of a single global admission window or token-bucket only, this approach combines predictive short-lived reservations with staged defer-and-suggest semantics, providing both predictable small guarantees and client-friendly guidance that enables graceful degradation and better autoscaler decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller grants leases per-tenant and emits lease events to metrics pipeline (lease.granted, lease.revoked, lease.adjusted)
2) For synthetic spike tests (3x baseline for 20s) tenants with active leases maintain >= 80% of configured soft-floor throughput while non-lease tenants see prioritized shedding
3) Autoscaler receives leased_util_pct signal and does not scale up in response to transient spikes shorter than lease duration in 90% of simulated episodes
4) Client receives structured defer response with Retry-After and suggested fallback in 100% of staged-defer cases
5) No latency regression >5th percentile for fast-path requests compared to baseline under identical load profiles
6) Rollout can be toggled per-cluster/region and has a clear kill-switch that returns all behavior to current admission controller
design_notes: Lease length: default 3s for interactive routes, 10s for steady streaming. Configurable at per-route or per-tenant policy level.
Prediction model: lightweight EWMA on per-tenant recent throughput (1s and 5s windows) with decay factor configurable; no ML service required.
Capacity accounting: treat leased slots as reserved headroom for autoscaler and runtime admission (i.e., leased slots reduce available concurrency for new unleased requests).
Reclamation strategy: proportional shrink based on deficit ratio; prefer reducing non-fast-path leases first.
Structured client guidance: use HTTP 202 (Accepted) with JSON body {lease_token, next_retry_ms, suggested_model, reason_code} or 429 with same payload for hard rejections.
Metrics: lease.count, lease.duration_histogram, lease_revocations, leased_util_pct, deferred_count_by_reason.
Interaction with KV cache and batching: leased requests are tagged; runtime keeps KV cache warm for active leases and prioritizes batching for lease-aligned windows to preserve latency guarantees.
test_plan: Unit tests for lease calculator and EWMA weight boundary conditions
Integration tests simulating mixed-tenant workloads with configurable lease floors and eviction thresholds
Chaos tests: forcibly revoke leases and validate client-facing messages and autoscaler behavior
Load tests in staging with realistic prompt/token distributions to validate 95/99p latency and throughput preservation
E2E test for rollback: enable controller only via feature-flag and prove kill-switch returns system to previous admission decisions within 30s
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout to internal canary cluster (alpha) for 48h
Gradual enablement by tenant tier: internal -> dev/test customers -> 10% of prod nodes -> 50% -> full region
Monitoring checks at each step: lease event rate sanity, latency p95, autoscaler scale events per minute
If errors exceed thresholds or customer impact > medium, kill feature-flag and notify SRE and product
Post-rollout: enable 30d retention for lease events in console for troubleshooting and customer reports
metrics: SLO: <=1% unexpected hard rejections for paying tenants with active leases
Target: leased_util_pct noise < 10% (stable within minute windows)
Latency: fast-path p50 <= baseline p50, p95 increase <= 10% under 2x load
Autoscaler: scale-up frequency attributable to transient spikes reduces by >=30% in A/B test
Observability: all lease lifecycle events sampled to traces at 1% by default
